blocks.content: A DaemonSet ensures exactly one copy of a Pod runs on every node in the cluster (or a chosen subset), automatically adjusting as nodes are added or removed, the standard tool for node-level agents.

Unlike a Deployment, which you tell to run a specific number of replicas, a DaemonSet has a different goal entirely: exactly one matching Pod, on every single node, regardless of how many nodes that actually is.

blocks.alt: Coverage across every node, not a chosen replica count

blocks.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-collector
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: collector
          image: log-collector:1.0

blocks.content: When a new node joins the cluster, exactly the node registration process covered in the Architecture module, the DaemonSet automatically schedules a new Pod there too, no manual intervention or scaling command required.

blocks.alt: Coverage extends automatically the moment a new node exists

blocks.content: The reverse happens just as automatically, when a node is removed from the cluster, its DaemonSet Pod is removed along with it, the DaemonSet's Pod count always tracks the current node count precisely.

blocks.alt: Coverage shrinks automatically too, always tracking the real node count

blocks.content: This is the cleanest way to remember the distinction: a Deployment maintains a fixed replica count you choose, a DaemonSet maintains one replica per node, whatever that count currently happens to be, two genuinely different goals.

blocks.alt: A chosen fixed count versus a count that tracks the cluster itself

blocks.content: DaemonSets fit anything that genuinely needs to run on every node: log collection agents (shipping each node's logs elsewhere), node-level monitoring agents (gathering per-node metrics), and even core cluster infrastructure like CNI plugins or kube-proxy itself, covered in the Architecture module, which commonly run as DaemonSets.

blocks.alt: Node-level agents, exactly the workload shape this object type is built for

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A DaemonSet runs exactly one matching Pod per node, automatically adding or removing Pods as the cluster's actual node count changes.
It is the standard tool for node-level agents, log collectors, monitoring agents, and core networking components like kube-proxy itself.
